ai.literal: Giving, fame-arising living; other than that, profit there is not to life.
ai.translation: Giving to others and living a life of fame: other than this, there is no true profit for a living soul.
ai.modern: பிறருக்குக் கொடுத்துப் புகழ் உண்டாகும்படி வாழ்வதைத் தவிர, மனித உயிருக்கு வேறு எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate purpose of human life as generosity and the good reputation it brings. The word 'ītal' means giving to those in need, while 'icaipaṭa' means causing fame to arise. The poet asserts that apart from this noble way of living, there is no other 'ūtiyam' or lasting profit for a living being. Fame earned through giving is presented as the only true wealth one can accumulate in life.

ai.literal: Speakers / things spoken / all / to those who ask / something / those who give / upon / stands / fame.
ai.translation: All the words of praise spoken in this world are simply the fame that rests upon those who give to the needy.
ai.modern: உலகத்தில் புகழ்ந்து பேசுபவர்கள் சொல்லும் சொற்கள் எல்லாம், வறுமையால் கேட்பவர்களுக்கு ஒரு பொருளைக் கொடுப்பவர்களின் மேல் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் புகழே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true nature and subject of praise in the world. The phrase 'உரைப்பார் உரைப்பவை எல்லாம்' (all that speakers speak) refers to all words of praise uttered by people. The poet asserts that all such praise ultimately belongs to 'ஈவார்' (those who give) who provide 'ஒன்று' (something) to 'இரப்பார்' (those who ask or beg). Thus, true fame rests solely on the act of generous giving to those in need, making charity the ultimate source of glory.

ai.literal: Matchless in the world exalted fame except, without perishing that which stands one thing is not.
ai.translation: Except for exalted, matchless fame, there is not a single thing in the world that stands without perishing.
ai.modern: ஒப்பற்ற உயர்ந்த புகழைத் தவிர, இவ்வுலகில் அழியாமல் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் பொருள் வேறு ஒன்றும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the impermanence of all worldly things compared to the enduring nature of true fame. The word 'oṉṟā' describes fame as matchless or without equal. Everything else in the world eventually perishes, as indicated by 'poṉṟātu' (without perishing). Therefore, achieving exalted fame is the only way to leave a lasting legacy that stands forever.

words.gloss: within the limits of the earth

ai.literal: Within the limits of the earth, if enduring fame is achieved, the wise ones it will not praise, the world of gods.
ai.translation: If a person achieves enduring fame within the limits of this earth, the celestial world of gods will praise them rather than its own wise sages.
ai.modern: இந்த நிலவுலகில் ஒருவன் நிலைத்த புகழைப் பெற்றால், தேவர் உலகம் தன் அறிஞர்களைப் போற்றாமல் அந்தப் புகழுடையவனையே போற்றும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of earthly fame. If a person earns lasting fame within the boundaries of this world, their greatness is recognized even in the heavens. The celestial world of gods will cease praising its own wise sages and instead celebrate the famous mortal. The word 'pulavar' here refers to the wise ones or sages of the heavenly realm, emphasizing that earthly fame outshines even celestial wisdom.

ai.literal: Prosperity-like ruin and existence-becoming death, to the wise except, is rare.
ai.translation: A ruin that resembles prosperity and a death that becomes an enduring existence are rare to achieve, except for the truly wise.
ai.modern: வளர்ச்சியைப் போன்ற ஒரு வீழ்ச்சியும், நிலைத்து வாழ்தலைத் தரும் ஒரு மரணமும் சிறந்த அறிஞர்களுக்கு அல்லாமல் மற்றவர்களுக்குக் கிடைப்பது அரிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the unique nature of fame achieved by the truly great. It speaks of a 'ruin' (loss of wealth or life) that acts like 'prosperity' because it brings lasting glory. Similarly, it describes a 'death' that becomes an 'existence' because the person lives on forever in memory. Such paradoxical achievements are impossible except for the wise who know how to live and die for a noble cause.

ai.literal: If appearing, with fame let one appear; those without that, than appearing, not appearing is good.
ai.translation: If you appear in this world, appear with fame. For those who lack it, it is better not to appear at all than to appear.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் உலகில் பிறந்து வாழ்ந்தால் புகழோடு வாழ வேண்டும். அந்தப் புகழ் இல்லாதவர்கள் உலகில் தோன்றுவதை விடத் தோன்றாமல் இருப்பதே நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute value of fame in human life. The word 'தோன்று' (appear) is used here to mean coming into existence or stepping onto the public stage of life. The poet declares that if one is to be born or make an appearance in the world, it must be accompanied by fame. For those who lack such fame, the text starkly states that non-existence is far better than existing without renown.

ai.literal: Fame-arising those-who-live-not themselves-blame-not; themselves those-who-despise blaming what?
ai.translation: Those who do not live a life worthy of fame do not blame themselves. What is the point of them blaming those who despise them?
ai.modern: புகழ் உண்டாகும்படி வாழாதவர்கள் தங்கள் குறையை எண்ணித் தங்களை நொந்துகொள்ள மாட்டார்கள். ஆனால், தங்களை இகழ்ந்து பேசுபவர்களை அவர்கள் நொந்துகொள்வதால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: The couplet addresses those who fail to live a life worthy of fame. Instead of recognizing their own flaws and blaming themselves, they often get angry at others who mock them. The poet asks what purpose it serves to blame their critics. The word 'தந்நோவார்' means they will not blame themselves, highlighting their lack of self-reflection. 'நோவது' refers to the act of blaming or feeling pain, emphasizing the misdirected resentment towards their detractors.

words.gloss: to the people of the world

ai.literal: Blame, they say, to the people of the world all, fame called remainder not obtaining if they fail.
ai.translation: If the people of the world fail to achieve the lasting legacy called fame, it is said to be a disgrace to them all.
ai.modern: இவ்வுலகில் வாழும் மக்கள் அனைவரும் புகழ் என்னும் எச்சத்தைப் பெறாமல் போனால், அது அவர்களுக்குப் பெரும் பழி என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: The couplet emphasizes that fame is the only true legacy a person leaves behind after death. The word 'eccam' literally means 'remainder' or 'that which survives', pointing to the enduring nature of a good reputation. If people fail to acquire this lasting fame, their very existence is considered a disgrace ('vasai'). Thus, living without earning a good name is seen as a fundamental failure in life.

ai.literal: blame without abundant yield will decrease fame without body that bore earth
ai.translation: The earth that bears a body destitute of fame will shrink in its flawless, abundant yield.
ai.modern: புகழ் இல்லாத மனிதர்களின் உடம்பைச் சுமந்த நிலமானது, தன்னுடைய குற்றமற்ற வளமான விளைச்சலில் குறைந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet connects human renown with the fertility of the earth. It states that if the earth has to bear the weight of a person who lives without fame, it will suffer a loss in its own natural abundance. The phrase 'வசை இலா வண்பயன்' refers to the flawless, rich yield of the land. By contrasting a blameless harvest with a fameless existence, the poet suggests that a life lived without earning good repute is a burden so unnatural that it blights the very ground it walks upon.

ai.literal: Blame ceasing those who live indeed they live; fame ceasing those who live indeed those who do not live.
ai.translation: Only those who live without blame truly live. Those who live without fame are as good as dead.
ai.modern: பழி இல்லாமல் வாழ்பவர்களே உண்மையாக வாழ்பவர்கள். புகழ் இல்லாமல் வாழ்பவர்கள் உயிருடன் இருந்தாலும் வாழாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts a life of blame with a life of fame. The word vasai means blame or reproach, and living without it is the mark of true life. Conversely, isai means fame or good reputation. The poet asserts that those who exist without earning a good reputation do not truly live at all, equating a fameless existence to not being alive.
